gaps.criterion: Rollback disables the moment a downstream governed action occurs
gaps.gap: The RULE is implemented and stated: ROLLBACK_BLOCKED_TEXT enumerates the three reasons a rollback closes - window_expired, downstream_action, already_rolled_back - with downstream_action explaining that reversing after somebody has acted would retract a record they have already used, and the screen states the 24-hour window closes early on such an action. The button is disabled. What is NOT proven is the TRANSITION, because nothing in this build can commit a run: sdk-import owns the commit and no LeadFlow write surface exists for it (the same missing surface recorded against task 75 AC1). So there is no committed run to act downstream upon, and the disable-on-action edge cannot be exercised. The mapping from run state to reason lives in one place ready for the commit endpoint to report it. Closing this needs the LeadFlow import write surface, after which a scenario can commit, trigger a downstream send, and assert the rollback has closed.

scenarios: The impact grid and commit plan are stated before committing
